segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK, so we've been looking at the attitudes of various social and cultural groups towards the management of their personal finances- how important they feel it is to save money, and what they save their money for.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One aspect that we haven't yet considered is gender.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So if we consider gender issues we're basically asking whether men and women have different attitudes towards saving money, and whether they save money for different things.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Back in 1928 the British writer George Bernard Shaw wrote in his Intelligent Women's Guide to Socialism and Capitalism that 'A man is supposed to understand politics, economics and finance and is therefore unwilling to accept essential instruction.' He also said, 'A woman, having fewer pretensions, is far more willing to learn'.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, though these days people might question a lot of the assumptions contained in those statements, recent research does suggest that there are some quite fundamental differences between men and women in their attitudes to economic matters.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let's look at what men and women actually save for.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Research studies of women in North America have found that women are far more likely to save for their children's education and they are also more likely to save up in order to buy a house one day.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The same studies have found that men, on the other hand, tend to save for~. which by the way takes a surprisingly large amount of the household budget in North America.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But the other main priority for men when saving money is their retirement.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When they're earning, they're far more likely to put money aside for their old age than women are.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now this is rather disturbing, because in fact the need for women to save for their old age is far greater than for men.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let's consider this for a moment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: To start with, it is a fact that throughout the world, women are likely to live many years longer than men, so they need money to support them during this time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Since women are likely to be the ones left without a partner in old age, they may therefore have to pay for nursing care, because they don't have a spouse to look after them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Furthermore the high divorce rates in North America are creating a poverty cycle for women.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It is the divorced women who will most often have to look after the children and thus they need more money to look after not just themselves but others.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So what can be done about this situation?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The population in North America is likely to contain an increasing number of elderly women.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The research indicates that at present for women it takes a crisis to make them think about their future financial situation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But of course this is the very worst time for anyone to make important decisions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Women today need to look ahead, think ahead- not wait until they're under pressure.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Even women in their early twenties need to think about pensions, for , and with increasing numbers of women in professional positions there are signs that this is beginning to happen.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then research also suggests that women avoid dealing effectively with their economic situation because of a lack of confidence.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The best way for them to overcome this is by getting themselves properly informed so they are less dependent on other people's advice.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A number of initiatives have been set up to help them do this.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This College, for , is one of the educational institutions which offers night classes in Money Management, and increasing numbers of women are enrolling on such courses.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Here, they can be given advice on different ways of saving.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Many women are unwilling to invest in stocks and shares, for instance, but these can be extremely profitable.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It is usually advised that at least 70% of a person's savings should be in low-risk investments but for the rest, financial advisors often advise taking some well-informed risks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Initiatives such as this can give women the economic skills and knowledge they need for a comfortable, independent retirement.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The increasing proportion of elderly women in the population is likely to have other economic consequences ...
